Kapow! Female Superheroes Are Breaking Comics Glass Ceiling

Just a question for discussion. Women have had female superheros for a very long time. If you look back through comic books such as Wonderwoman, Xena, Boudicca...(probably too small for many to know about), The Justice League of America, Ametheyst, Bulleteer, the white witch, Crimson Fox, Cyclone...and those are the ones just off the top of my head...from comics I have read as a little girl and since.

How is it that there is a glass ceiling on females being portrayed in comics? To be honest, I have always thought that we are equally represented in comics, especially since the 60's. Perhaps, my mother sheltered me and didn't allow me to experience or see the same things you have and I would really like to know why some feel there is a glass ceiling in comics.

A Vocativ analysis of Marvel’s database found nearly three times as many male characters as female characters that have gotten their own series—118 compared to 38—and more than twice as many male than female characters generally. (For the sake of comparison, only characters from Marvel’s “main” universe, Earth-616, were analyzed, and they were only scored as having received their own books if they didn’t share it with another character, if their name was featured in the title and if it ran for at least two issues. The analysis relied on Marvel’s internal data, which may be incomplete in places.)

Relavent bit of the article (emphasis mine).

Though I'm wondering when exactly the shift occurred, since the numbers look more or less even right now.

This is tangential, but I'm a man, and I really want a Black Widow movie. She's got to have a more interesting back story than "Got kidnapped and made metal suit" or "Was weak so government gave super steroids," or "is a god." They're missing a major opportunity.

I agree; I'd love to see a movie with Black Widow as the main character. But did you see the backlash that the latest Avengers movie got when they went into her backstory? That wasn't the only component of the criticism, not by a long shot. There wasn't an aspect of Widow's depiction that wasn't vocally criticized.

Now, personally speaking, I'd be hesitant to try and write a BW movie; I don't know if I could make anything that would appease the masses and still be true to the comic character.

This is great (love the new batgirl design for example), but I often wish that there were more original female superheroes (superheroines?), rather than cut/paste versions of male superheroes. Rather than batman and batgirl, or thor and "female thor" (what an awful name), it'd be cool to have some names that didn't have "woman" or "girl" tacked on the end to identify them as a woman. X-men (despite the series' name) does this well with characters like Storm.

Anyway, regardless of my thoughts on it, great article :) It's awesome to see women in comics with decent outfits. Women don't need holes in their shirts to be sexy.
